cultural.vision_reason: This is a wooden Kuba ndop royal figure with characteristic headdress, cowrie shell belt, game board, and ceremonial knife — a classic Kuba carved wood sculpture, correctly attributed to the culture but mislabeled as metalwork (it is wood, not metal).

physical.title: figure
physical.summary: Male king figure (ndop) made of wood. Figure sits crosslegged on a square platform (yiing) carved with representation of a creeper vine. In front of the king is three-row game board (lele). He holds a ceremonial knife in his left hand. He wears a distinctive projecting hoe-shaped headddress decorated with carved cowrie shells around the edge and an interlocking pattern known as 'woot' on the top surface. Other key items of regalia include the representation of a circular neck ring, cane shoulder hoops, cloth plaque covering the buttocks and a belt with three rows of cowrie shells. Relief surfaces have red camwood deposits.
